A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Moving Out and BASS. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and matchable despite substantial layout changes and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original dataset analyses, AI-AI evaluations, human-AI experiments and questionnaires, and extensive appendix ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains those original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, visual-input evaluations, and additional methodological analyses.

M1.justification: The main augmentation, dynamics prediction, and action-selection pipeline is retained. Appendices M and S add tested extensions using visual observations and a time-contrastive learned progress estimator instead of the original geometric progress score.

E1.justification: v4 adds a raw-image observation scenario on Map 6. Both versions retain the twelve Moving Out maps, two challenges, and Overcooked Cramped Room experiment. Discussion of additional agents or objects does not establish evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: CoMeDi is newly evaluated alongside MAPPO and DP/BASS on Maps 1 and 12 in v4 Table 8; its underlying work was only cited in v3. The original main baseline suite and dynamics-model comparators remain.

E3.justification: Human-study reporting changes from 32 to 12 maps per participant in Section 6.1 and from 12 to 32 volunteers in the appendix, resolving inconsistencies without establishing a rerun. New targeted protocols include four pose-noise levels and 2,000 sampled validations using 80 trajectories. Original splits, metrics, and training budgets remain.

E4.justification: v4 adds single-agent versus multi-agent recombination and simulation ablations, pose-noise validity and sensitivity tests, visual-observation comparisons, and learned progress-estimator analysis. These substantially extend testing of coordination mechanisms, augmentation feasibility, and dependence on structured observations and geometric scoring beyond v3's retained ablations.

E5.justification: Appendix O.3 newly specifies 2,000 samples for validity estimation and a nominal 99% interval of approximately [-0.005, 0.005] for Gaussian pose noise. This interval characterizes injected noise. Existing 20-run averaging, standard-error tables, and the survey t-test remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Main Table 2 and earlier appendix results retain their values, while v4 adds substantial results for the new comparisons and analyses. Examples include unseen Map 1 TCR of 0.3768 for CoMeDi versus 0.7080 for DP/BASS, and pose-noise validity falling from 99.87% at sigma 0.002 to 35.01% at 0.02. These are additional findings, not improvements over v3 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: Appendix O.2 introduces an explicit mathematical compatibility condition for the single-agent recombination control: matching either the initial or final state, contrasted with BASS requiring both. The original Dec-MDP formulation, metric definitions, and recombination equations remain; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the principal contributions: a physically grounded collaboration benchmark, two challenges with human demonstrations, and BASS improving collaborative adaptability. Rewritten wording and additional supporting experiments do not materially change these central claims.

C2.justification: v4 substantially expands mechanism and applicability discussion. It links dense rewards to homogeneous ZSC motion, argues for explicit multi-agent coupling, identifies recombination difficulties with more agents, explains noise-related failures and resimulation costs, and acknowledges missing theoretical guarantees. Appendix S additionally argues that environment rewards are unnecessary.

D1.justification: v4 adds descriptions of visual encoding, progress scoring through embedding distance from the initial observation, and simulator replay for noise validation. Original grid discretization, default noise magnitude, optimizer settings, hardware, inference timings, and project access information remain.

R1.justification: v4 replaces the MAGICAL/XIRL attribution with a direct Pymunk citation and adds VAE, TCL, and R3M references. Table 3 expands comparisons with HumanTHOR and Habitat, while the CoMeDi discussion sharpens positioning against ZSC. Most cited works remain despite bibliographic formatting updates.

P1.justification: Rewrites concentrate on the abstract, introduction, augmentation explanation, and future-work discussion. Tasks become challenges, research questions expand, appendix material is regrouped, and an Impact Statement is added. The overall section sequence and most existing technical appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column ICML main paper, with extensive resizing and relocation of existing displays. The environment illustration is reworked, physical-attribute and recombination illustrations and TCL plots are added, and comparison and analysis tables expand.

improvement.justification: v4 strengthens evidence for BASS's multi-agent design, augmentation validity, and broader applicability, while correcting inconsistent human-study counts. These improve support and reporting beyond v3's already extensive evaluation. The gains remain limited by selected-map extensions and inconsistent descriptions of endpoint matching between Section 5.1 and Appendix R.1.
